newsitem.title: UK: UK's OFT says Premier League acting as a cartel.
newsitem.headline: UK's OFT says Premier League acting as a cartel.

text.p: The head of Britain's Office of Fair Trading (OFT) said on Tuesday that English soccer's Premier League clubs were restricting choice and inflating prices in the way they sell television rights.

"The current system of collective and exclusive selling has resulted in severe restrictions on the number of Premier League matches shown on television, and in artificially high prices for those that are televised," said John Bridgeman, Director General of Fair Trading.
Speaking at a conference, Bridgeman said the 20 clubs in the Premier League were effectively acting as a cartel by selling rights collectively rather than individually.
Bridgeman has referred the Premier League's television deal with BSkyB Plc and the BBC to the Restrictive Practices Court. The deal, worth a total of 743 million stg, runs until 2001.

He said the case should be heard next year but added that appeals mean it could be years before it is finally settled. The Court could outlaw the deal, making clubs negotiate their own individual arrangements.
"I do not wish to see the Premier League broken up," Bridgeman said.
But he said the rights of armchair sports fans had to be safeguarded.
"Sport is big business, sport on television is further big business and, as they both develop, the interests of consumers need to be protected," he added.
